_meta.indication: GOMEKLI is indicated for the treatment of adult and pediatric patients 2 years of age and older with neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1) who have symptomatic plexiform neurofibromas (PN) not amenable to complete resection

pivotal_trials.trial_name: ReNeu study (also referred to as Study MEK-NF-201)
pivotal_trials.phase: Phase 2b (ReNeu / Study MEK-NF-201 is an open-label, multi-center, Phase 2b study)
pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, single-arm study; patients received GOMEKLI 2 mg/m2 orally twice daily for the first 21 days of each 28-day cycle until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity
pivotal_trials.population: Patients ≥ 2 years of age with symptomatic, inoperable neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1) associated plexiform neurofibromas (PN) causing significant morbidity
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Confirmed overall response rate (ORR), defined as percentage of patients with complete response or partial response (≥20% reduction in PN volume), by BICR per REiNS criteria; secondary endpoint duration of response
pivotal_trials.result: Confirmed ORR: adults 41% (95% CI 29, 55); pediatric 52% (95% CI 38, 65). DoR ≥12 months: 88% (adults), 90% (pediatric); DoR ≥24 months: 50% (adults), 48% (pediatric)

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (>25%): rash, diarrhea, nausea, musculoskeletal pain, vomiting, and fatigue (adults); rash, diarrhea, musculoskeletal pain, abdominal pain, vomiting, headache, paronychia, left ventricular dysfunction, and nausea (pediatric). Most common Grade 3/4 laboratory abnormality (>2%) was increased creatine phosphokinase (plus decreased neutrophil count in pediatric). Rash occurred in 84% of patients.
target_moa: Mirdametinib is an inhibitor of mitogen-activated protein kinase kinases 1 and 2 (MEK1/2), upstream regulators of the ERK pathway; it inhibited MEK1/2 kinase activity and downstream phosphorylation of ERK
companion_dx_detail: No devices or companion diagnostic issues (NA)

advisory_committee.vote: FDA did not refer this application to an advisory committee because it did not raise significant public health questions regarding the role of mirdametinib for the proposed indication

orphan_indication.text: Orphan Drug designation granted 30 Oct 2018 for mirdametinib for treatment of NF1

basis.text: Rare Pediatric Disease designation granted 24 Jul 2023; mirdametinib for treatment of NF1 designated as drug for a rare pediatric disease

citations.quote: 24-Jul-2023	Rare Pediatric Disease Designation Granted Letter	Mirdametinib for treatment of NF1 is designated as drug for a rare pediatric disease.

summary.text: GOMEKLI (mirdametinib) received regular approval under a Priority review NDA for NF1-associated symptomatic plexiform neurofibromas not amenable to complete surgical resection, based primarily on ORR and DoR from the single-arm ReNeu study. The program held Orphan Drug (30Oct2018), Fast Track (28May2019), and Rare Pediatric Disease (24Jul2023) designations.

citations.quote: The review team recommends regular approval of mirdametinib for the treatment of adult and pediatric patients 2 years of age and older with neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1) who have symptomatic plexiform neurofibromas not amenable to complete surgical resection. The recommendation for approval is primarily supported by overall response rate (ORR) and duration of response (DOR) results from Study MEK

requirement.text: 4784-3 Conduct an integrated safety analysis of data from clinical trials to further characterize the long-term incidence, severity, and outcomes of the known serious risks of ocular toxicity, left ventricular dysfunction, and dermatologic adverse reactions. Include the long-term follow-up safety data (minimum of 7 years) from adult and pediatric patients enrolled on the MEK-NF-201 (ReNeu) trial (NCT03962543) and all other ongoing and completed trials of mirdametinib to include an analysis of the following toxicities: ocular toxicity (including but not limited to retinal pigment epithelial detachment and retinal vein occlusion), cardiac toxicity (including but not limited to left ventricular dysfunction), and serious dermatologic toxicity.
